questions.q: [NSMO of KSA — Stage 1 Screening] Evaluate the exact telescoping radical sum \[ \sum_{k=1}^{15} \frac{1}{\sqrt{k + 1} + \sqrt{k}}. \]
questions.answer: Rationalizing each denominator by multiplying by \( \sqrt{k+1} - \sqrt{k} \) gives \( \frac{1}{\sqrt{k+1} + \sqrt{k}} = \sqrt{k+1} - \sqrt{k} \). Telescoping from \( k = 1 \) to \( 15 \) leaves \( \sqrt{16} - \sqrt{1} = 4 - 1 = 3 \).

questions.q: [NSMO of KSA — Stage 2 Regional] Compute the exact value of the finite series \[ \sum_{k=1}^{8} \frac{2}{(2k - 1)(2k + 1)}. \]
questions.answer: Using partial fractions, \( \frac{2}{(2k - 1)(2k + 1)} = \frac{2}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2k - 1} - \frac{1}{2k + 1}\right) \). Telescoping from \( k = 1 \) to \( 8 \) gives \[ \frac{2}{2}\left(1 - \frac{1}{17}\right) = \frac{2}{2} \cdot \frac{16}{17} = \frac{16}{17}. \]

questions.q: [NSMO of KSA — Stage 2 Qualifier] Using the quartic factorization \( k^4 + k^2 + 1 = (k^2 - k + 1)(k^2 + k + 1) \), evaluate the exact sum \[ \sum_{k=1}^{5} \frac{k}{k^4 + k^2 + 1}. \]
questions.answer: Since \( (k^2 + k + 1) - (k^2 - k + 1) = 2k \), \[ \frac{k}{k^4 + k^2 + 1} = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{k^2 - k + 1} - \frac{1}{k^2 + k + 1}\right). \] Notice \( (k+1)^2 - (k+1) + 1 = k^2 + k + 1 \), so the sum telescopes cleanly from \( k = 1 \) to \( 5 \): \[ \frac{1}{2}\left(1 - \frac{1}{5^2 + 5 + 1}\right) = \frac{15}{31}. \]

questions.answer: Since \( (k^2 + k + 1) - (k^2 - k + 1) = 2k \), \[ \frac{k}{k^4 + k^2 + 1} = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{k^2 - k + 1} - \frac{1}{k^2 + k + 1}\right). \] Notice \( (k+1)^2 - (k+1) + 1 = k^2 + k + 1 \), so the sum telescopes cleanly from \( k = 1 \) to \( 6 \): \[ \frac{1}{2}\left(1 - \frac{1}{6^2 + 6 + 1}\right) = \frac{21}{43}. \]

questions.q: [NSMO of KSA — Stage 1 Screening] Positive integers \( x \) and \( y \) satisfy \( \gcd(x, y) = 3 \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(x, y) = 180 \). What is the **minimum** possible value of \( x + y \)?
questions.answer: Write \( x = 3u \) and \( y = 3v \) with \( \gcd(u, v) = 1 \). Then \( \operatorname{lcm}(x, y) = 3uv = 180 \implies uv = 60 \). Among coprime factor pairs of \( 60 \), the pair closest to \( \sqrt{60} \) minimizes \( u + v = 17 \), giving \( x + y = 3(17) = 51 \).

questions.answer: Write \( x = 4u \) and \( y = 4v \) with \( \gcd(u, v) = 1 \). Then \( \operatorname{lcm}(x, y) = 4uv = 336 \implies uv = 84 \). Among coprime factor pairs of \( 84 \), the pair closest to \( \sqrt{84} \) minimizes \( u + v = 19 \), giving \( x + y = 4(19) = 76 \).
